content:
Alex: quick q — staging telemetry pods (namespace telemetry-staging) are losing AWS creds after ~11–13h. Seen in a few uploader jobs. Any recent changes to SA token TTLs?
Sam: noted, saw one alert. not a rollout I'm aware of. what error do you get?
Alex: aws SDK errors: InvalidIdentityToken / expired token. logs show token refresh succeeds briefly, then fails later.
Mikayla: do you mean the projected serviceAccount token expires? kube version is 1.25 in staging, right?
Alex: yeah 1.25. I can paste an example from a crashloop: 
```
2026-03-16T21:12:09Z ERROR s3 Upload failed: Token expired
... token valid until 2026-03-17T08:00:00Z
... subsequent token request returned 401
```
Jordan: sounds like the bound SA token TTL is shorter than the app expects OR there's a refresh race. Are pods using the projected token path (volumeToken) or calling TokenRequest from app?
Alex: they're using default projected volume token (automount true) via k8s serviceaccount (no explicit TokenRequest). We also have IRSA annotation on the SA.
Sam: FYI we recently applied a cluster-level policy that set TokenRequest ttl to 1h for short-lived tokens for a different namespace — maybe that leaked?
Mikayla: ok two things to check: the SA automount and the projected token expiry vs AWS STS expiration. EKS/IRSA uses the projected token to call sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity — that token itself has an expiration embedded and the SDK uses it to mint creds which also expire. If the projected token rotates unpredictably, apps that cache creds might face gaps.
Alex: any Terraform knobs we can change quickly?
Mikayla: yes — if you manage the SA with k8s provider in TF, you can set the projected token ttl via the TokenRequest API client side, but the SA annotation approach doesn't control TTL. For a quick workaround set automountServiceAccountToken: false on pods that don't need k8s API, then have a sidecar or init that does explicit TokenRequest with a longer TTL.
Jordan: example TF snippet (very minimal):
```
# create SA
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "telemetry_uploader" {
  metadata {
    name = "telemetry-uploader"
    namespace = "telemetry-staging"
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.telemetry.arn
    }
  }
}
# pod uses automount: false, sidecar will call TokenRequest
```
Sam: if you want to try a cluster-scoped change, kube apiserver has a --service-account-issuer and projection configs but we don't manage that in TF here. I'd avoid changing API server flags.
Alex: got it. For immediate mitigation, I'll flip automount to false in the deployment and add a small sidecar that does TokenRequest with ttl 8h. Anyone object?
Mikayla: :+1: test in staging only. Also add kubelet logs for token rotation to your incident notes.
Jordan: one more gotcha — ensure the sidecar uses the same IRSA role ARN (same SA) and doesn't create new creds concurrently. Race conditions happen when multiple processes try to refresh.
Alex: noted. I'll open a short PR with the deployment patch and sidecar container image (lightweight token-proxy). pinging @Sam @Mikayla for review when ready.
Sam: :eyes: will review after standup.
deploy-bot: Deployment check — new manifest change detected for telemetry-staging/telemetry-uploader, required: open PR and pass unit + e2e.
Alex: thanks. I'll keep thread updated with logs and PR link.
Mikayla: also add a note in the namespace README about why automount was disabled and how token rotation works — helps future debugging.
Alex: will do. thanks all.
